name: Dutertismo
summary: Dutertismo is the personalist, authoritarian-populist politics built around Rodrigo Duterte, president of the Philippines from 2016 to 2022. It combines penal populism (the war on drugs, restoring the death penalty), a strong militarized executive, Filipino nationalism with an independent, China-friendly foreign policy, federalism, hostility to political elites and intellectuals, and populist social pledges such as free state-college tuition and universal health coverage.
scope: The profile represents the Duterte movement as it existed around his 2016-2022 presidency and since, as described in the Wikipedia article on Dutertismo, his inaugural address and scholarship on his penal populism. It covers the core shared by his loyal supporters and does not cover the broader Philippine populist tradition or the personal views of individual allies. Because it is a movement around one leader rather than a doctrine with a canon, many social and economic questions were never addressed and are answered at low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Build Build Build, martial law in Mindanao, Anti-Terrorism Act, ICC withdrawal, free tuition and Bangsamoro law.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Universal health coverage was among Duterte's 2016 campaign promises as the sources list them, and his government backed it, so a Dutertista agrees.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from his campaign pledges on pay and ending contractualization; no source quotes him on raising the minimum wage substantially.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: he liberalized foreign investment rules yet ran a state-heavy, populist programme, so adherents lean neither way clearly.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the article notes strongly Chinese-linked firms taking grid stakes under him and no push for nationalization; his rhetoric targeted oligarchs rather than private ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: he spoke against pulling down the rich in his inaugural, but his rhetoric attacked oligarchs and he signed a tax reform law.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: he promised to end labor contractualization, which favours workers, but the movement is built around a leader rather than organized labor.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: his rule-of-law rhetoric supports property, yet he threatened to seize oligarch firms, leaving adherents without a clear line.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from his anti-oligarch attacks and promise to end contractualization, which imply tighter control of big business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from his populist promises of higher pensions and pay and free tuition, which point against cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources suggests worker-owned firms; his economics is state-led populism with private firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The movement favours security-state measures; his government signed the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020, which widened surveillance powers.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The drug war is the defining policy of the ideology and his inaugural vowed a relentless, sustained fight against illegal drugs, so legalization is rejected.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: he insulted critics and foreign bodies openly, which cuts against speech limits, though this is not a stated doctrine.

strong-leader.rationale: Scholarship ties the ideology to a charismatic strongman and cult of personality, and Kenny and Holmes link support for the drug war to preference for charismatic leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology is statist and authoritarian, with a state that kills and directs; his inaugural stresses what government must provide.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: the ideology favours state force but he also loosened ties to vigilante violence; the sources never mention gun control.

empower-police-military.rationale: The article lists militarism and state violence as core, and he appointed retired military officers widely and declared martial law in Mindanao.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from his tough-on-vice stance and conservative Philippine culture; no source gives a position.

decide-locally.rationale: Dutertist federalism is a named component, and he campaigned for decentralization, though adherents also centralize power in the president.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal populism holds that criminals should be punished harshly, and the drug war killed small-time users rather than treating them.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from Philippine Catholic culture and his stance as a conservative populist; his own conduct and remarks were mixed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Contested: Duterte voiced personal openness on LGBT rights at times, but his coalition is socially conservative and no policy was passed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from Philippine law and the Catholic majority base; the sources give no position of his.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents are split: he attacked Catholic bishops yet courted evangelical figures such as Quiboloy.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: the ideology does not frame politics around race; no relevant position in the sources.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from a populist-conservative base and his macho style; not addressed in the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The article describes the ideology as a mix of Filipino nationalism and neo-nationalism, so preserving national traditions is accepted.

gradual-change.rationale: He campaigned on "real change" and defied institutions, and the ideology is anti-establishment rather than incrementalist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred: it is not an immigration-focused movement, and the article faults Chinese-linked gaming operators rather than immigrants in general.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He attacked the UN, EU and ICC and withdrew the Philippines from the International Criminal Court, effective 2019.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: he opened foreign investment rules but also pursued nationalist, state-led growth, so adherents have no settled line.

nation-first.rationale: His independent foreign policy and nationalism put sovereignty first and he rejected outside criticism, though he sought Chinese investment.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He rejected Western human-rights claims as foreign and railed against interference, which cuts against intervention abroad.

open-borders.rationale: The nationalist, sovereigntist character of the ideology rules out open borders, as its attacks on foreign interference show.

limit-growth.rationale: His signature economic programme was Build Build Build, an infrastructure-led growth drive, which opposes limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: no source records a climate agenda; he criticized rich countries yet prioritized growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources about technology as a theme.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred: nuclear energy is not part of the ideology's documented platform.

revolution-justified.rationale: He cracked down on communist insurgents and ended peace talks, though he floated revolutionary government rhetoric; mostly opposed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anti-intellectualism is listed as a core element, so experts having more say than the public is rejected.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of communism at home and mixed market policy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: unaddressed in the sources; adherents have no clear line on worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: no source records any position on land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: no stated view; his rhetoric against oligarchs is the only hint.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: he promised higher pensions and pay but no source mentions an unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: he opened to foreign ownership while talking nationalism, so adherents are not clearly for tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from Build Build Build, the state-led infrastructure programme, and ties to state-owned Chinese capital.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources about small property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A statist, nationalist populism with an anti-communist stance at home has no place for abolishing money or wage labor.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: no source on monetary policy; his state-led growth drive points away from abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: no source discusses state-recognized labor bodies; the ideology is leader-centred, not corporatist in doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: He ruled through PDP-Laban and allies in a multiparty system, and the ideology is a personality cult rather than a single-party doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A republican presidential strongman movement rests on electoral mandate, so hereditary monarchy is not part of it.

democracy-best.rationale: Authoritarian populism holds that the leader's will can override procedure, and Kenny and Holmes find support tied to extrajudicial killing, so adherents prize results over democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: populists praise the people's will, but no source shows support for referendums by this movement.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement is leader-centred and anti-communist at home, so councils replacing parliaments are alien to it.

right-to-secede.rationale: He pushed federalism within one state and ran a martial-law campaign against separatists, so secession is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred: the cult of a strongman implies some are suited to rule, but no source states a doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The ideology is defined by state violence and the killings of drug suspects, so it rejects the claim that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: militarism is a core part but no source says war builds national character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Contested: he attacked the Catholic hierarchy yet courted religious leaders, and the sources give no line.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred: no scripture-based law programme in the sources; his rhetoric against bishops points against it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The ideology exalts the state's police and military, so privatizing courts and defense is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Militarism is listed as core and he appointed military figures widely, though he reduced reliance on the US.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The nationalism described is civic Filipino nationalism in a multi-ethnic archipelago, not an ethnic-nation doctrine.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Anti-communism is a named component, so Marxist class conflict as history's driver is rejected.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: his populism promises welfare but no source supports outcome equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His inaugural wanted indigenous peoples included in the peace process, but no source covers land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: no source records the movement claiming reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: no source records religion-based unions; his pro-China tilt is geopolitical.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred: the movement's nationalism and duty language run against a self-interest ethic, though nothing is stated.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He called human rights for criminals a Western concept that should not apply in the Philippines, putting order ahead of individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred: no environmental philosophy in the sources.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: no source on population control as part of the ideology; he did back family planning at times.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The ideology celebrates infrastructure and growth through Build Build Build, so it rejects this primitivist view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: not part of the documented platform.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred: not part of the documented platform.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: a personalist movement puts power in a leader, not algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the security-state outlook and Anti-Terrorism Act; encryption is not discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Inferred: it appeals to a lost order in the form of discipline, but also promises radical change.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement prizes results and tolerates unorthodox methods; the inaugural asks the public to judge his methods by outcomes against crime.

direct-action.rationale: He sought office via elections and ruled as president; the movement is not a direct-action tradition.

means-match-ends.rationale: The drug war used killing for a stated aim of safety, so adherents reject matching means to ends in that sense.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The ideology pursues modernization through infrastructure; foraging is alien to it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A statist, anti-communist ideology rejects this Marxist-anarchist aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: welfare pledges exist but he rejected communism at home.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the anti-communism; no economic doctrine stated.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The anti-communist component rejects the Marxist theory of exploitation, though he attacked oligarchs rhetorically.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-communism at home is a named component; he classed the CPP-NPA as terrorists.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization belongs to the communism the ideology opposes at home.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: not a theme in the sources; anti-communism points against it.

taxation-theft.rationale: He signed a tax reform law and funded programmes by taxes; the movement is statist.

harm-principle.rationale: The drug war punished private drug use, which a harm principle would not allow, and adherents defended it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He dismissed rights claims for criminals as a Western idea, so individual rights are not held as supreme.

conscription.rationale: Inferred: militarism supports it but no source mentions the draft.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: leader-centred politics offers voice to the strongman, not exit as a check.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: not a theme in the sources.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred: abstract; his welfare pledges point slightly toward it but nothing is stated.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred from anti-intellectualism and his attacks on the press and universities; no source states it as a thesis.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred: no race science in the sources; nationalism is civic.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: the movement is personalist, not an organic-representation doctrine.

total-state.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian but not totalizing across culture and economy as described.

national-rebirth.rationale: He campaigned on "real change" against corruption and decay, and the ideology is a neo-nationalism of renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He set aside claims in the South China Sea and sought good ties with neighbours, so expansion is not a goal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: a cult of personality has personal loyalty to the leader, but no feudal oath doctrine.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bonded labor has no place in a modernizing populism that promised to end contractualization.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: anti-intellectual, but not a postmodern thesis; unaddressed.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred: contested; he rejected Western human rights claims as foreign.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred: no source states the doctrine.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred: the movement has no stated position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred: no stated position, though Duterte often spoke in Filipino and Cebuano.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred: not a theme in the sources.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: not documented; he backed free state-college tuition.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from his large Build Build Build spending, which relied on borrowing.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: the ideology subordinates freedom to order, but backs growth.

rule-by-example.rationale: Government in the ideology rests on force and punishment, as the drug war and penal populism show, not on moral example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism and an independent foreign policy assert Filipino sovereignty, though secessionist groups are opposed.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: he attacked the UN, but the ideology is not interventionist abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred from anti-intellectualism and populist emotion; not stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: nationalism implies priority to citizens; not addressed in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: His inaugural said government serves every citizen, not a class, and warned against pulling down the rich or the wage payer.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The neo-nationalist ideology values heritage; sacrificing museums is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: he distanced from the US and moved toward China and Russia, but not as a formal front.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Contested in practice: he made sexist remarks yet backed women in office; no doctrine in the sources.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: not documented; he courted finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Civic nationalism in the Philippines has no place for race segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The anti-communist component rejects this Marxist thesis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the growth focus and Build Build Build, which favours energy supply.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of replacement is not part of the ideology; the Philippines is not an immigration destination.

national-mission.rationale: He pursued an inward, independent foreign policy rather than spreading a model abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: he made dismissive remarks on women; not stated as doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-corruption and hostility to the political elite are central; his inaugural names corruption in the high and low echelons of government as a main problem.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits are not part of the ideology and clash with its populism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement rejects accountability for drug-war killings; he withdrew from the ICC and was arrested on an ICC warrant in 2025, which adherents denounce.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The inaugural expects the state to provide for those with little, and the ideology is interventionist.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No racial doctrine in the sources; civic Filipino nationalism rejects it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Drug suspects were treated as expendable by the policy, so adherents do not give all equal protection in practice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The movement is anti-communist at home and this debate is not its own.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: he signed the Bangsamoro Organic Law, recognizing separate Muslim arrangements, but no wider position.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: no source; a Catholic-majority populism has no such programme.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of Philippine politics or this movement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine alien to a movement that opposes communism at home.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Contested: he won with 39 percent and claims a popular mandate, yet adherents accept rule by force.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred: he opposed the Moro separatists but backed autonomy, not transfer.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The drug war is state violence against suspects before any aggression on their part, and adherents back it in surveys.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He designated the CPP-NPA a terrorist group and ended talks, which fits outlawing groups seeking to overthrow the order.

separated-powers.rationale: The ideology favours a dominant executive; his inaugural asked Congress and the Commission on Human Rights to allow his methods.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist doctrine rejected by an anti-communist movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His inaugural says government should provide for those who have little, and the movement runs on poor voters' support.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian bent, but he promised to end contractualization.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: not documented as a thesis.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: A strongman movement rejects lotteries for public office.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He declared martial law in Mindanao during the Marawi siege and signed the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020, using emergency powers.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: he attacked outlets such as ABS-CBN, but no one-party media system is part of the ideology.

party-commands-army.rationale: He wanted military loyal to himself and appointed veterans; the state, not a party, commands it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred: unaddressed; PDP-Laban discipline was personal.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His independent foreign policy and attacks on the EU and UN reject pooling sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential command of the armed forces was central to his style, with ex-military appointments and martial law in Mindanao.

clerical-rule.rationale: He attacked the Catholic hierarchy and rule by clerics is not part of the ideology.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement is nationalist and militarist; defeating one's own government is rejected.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Contested: he voiced charter change interest, but the 2016 and later sources give no stance.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Contested: he reduced reliance on the US and limited visiting troops, but did not end alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No such programme; alien to the ideology.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militarism favours a professional state force; an armed citizenry replacing it is not part of it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectualism is listed as a core element, which includes distrust of the educated elite.

death-penalty.rationale: He campaigned on restoring the death penalty, favouring hanging, and the article says restoration bills failed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: disciplined populism favours conformity; unaddressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from his independent foreign policy and economic nationalism; not stated.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He campaigned for federalism by rewriting the constitution and talked of a revolutionary government alternative.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian populism and his remarks on discipline for development; not stated as such.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: unaddressed; Philippines has no program.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He won direct presidential election with a personal mandate, and the ideology centres on a popular strongman.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He affirmed the arbitral ruling at the UN in 2020 on Philippine claims, though he set it aside earlier; the position has been sovereignty-first.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from his populist remarks on oligarchs and the duty of government to the poor; not stated as doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: Contested: he doubted US treaty commitments while keeping the alliance.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: he fought Catholic bishops but there is no stated doctrine.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ideology is a partisan, personalist leadership; a symbolic head above politics is the opposite.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He declared martial law and fought the Marawi siege and ended talks with armed rebels, which fits forceful unity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The cult of personality has leader worship but without divinity claims; unaddressed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: he signed a reform law but no flat tax position is documented.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Adherents defended his rule beyond normal limits, though his inaugural claimed uncompromising adherence to rule of law.

leader-cult.rationale: The article describes a cult of personality around Duterte, with the fist symbol and the green colour.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He kept to constitutional borders and the arbitral claims; irredentism is not part of it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not part of a Catholic-majority populism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: he signed the Bangsamoro Organic Law, though that is regional autonomy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist historical materialism is rejected by the anti-communist ideology.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from his anti-oligarch rhetoric and transparency pledges in the inaugural.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Penal populism treats popular majorities as legitimating the drug war against judicial restraint.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: he sought foreign investment and trade with China, so a closed bloc is not his aim.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He fought the NPA and labeled it terrorist.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from anti-oligarch populism; dynasties are in fact common among adherents.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He denounced Western interference and colonial legacies; tutelage is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Neo-nationalism and militarism support patriotic schooling; Duterte Youth is an affiliated organization.

delink-world-market.rationale: He courted foreign investment and Chinese trade; breaking economic ties is not the programme.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He dismissed rights claims for suspects and wanted to tone down the constitution, so entrenched limits on majorities are resisted.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rule rests on electoral mandate in a republic, not inheritance, as his own election shows.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Adherents defend the leader against opponents rather than endorse resisting him.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The ideology favours a strong executive, and his inaugural asked Congress to accommodate his mandate.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: his inaugural calls for providing for those with little but also warns against pulling down the rich.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A mass-mobilizing movement with a cult leader does not value withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: a critical-theory thesis the movement does not address.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: his anti-West rhetoric hints at it but no dependency theory is stated.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: the article faults Chinese nationals in firms, not offices; unaddressed.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: not applicable to an anti-communist ideology.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: he took Chinese loans and aid, so adherents are not clear on this.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: he set aside the South China Sea ruling at times, unaddressed otherwise.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: not part of the platform.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: a right-wing populist movement does not make it a founding value; Marcos burial shows disregard.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: anti-communist yet fond of Chinese communist government, so unclear.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from his Marcos burial in the Heroes' Cemetery.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He called human rights for criminals a Western concept unfit for the Philippines and rejected Western pressure on his methods.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Militarism and appointing retired officers to civilian posts show an expanded political role for the armed forces.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Filipino family culture; not stated.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: he appointed loyalists and veterans, so merit exams are not his emphasis.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Contested: he opened foreign ownership rules while criticizing Chinese-linked firms in the grid.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: leader-centred rule does not bind leaders to delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from his promise of higher pensions.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: his inaugural said he knew the limits of presidential power, but no budget view is stated.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: he spoke of higher foreign ownership of businesses; land is unaddressed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: His independent line rejects foreign meddling and he fought insurgents himself.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He opposed foreign interference and set aside the US alliance, so great power intervention is not endorsed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Attacks on oligarchs and the inaugural's call for transparency in contracts suggest agreement.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Anti-Terrorism Act and his attacks on NGOs and foreign critics.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: he promised pay raises but no job guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: He attacked Western democracies' lectures; democracy promotion is not his aim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The ideology prizes order and punishment, rejecting a right to disobey.

non-intervention.rationale: He rejected UN, EU and US interference in the Philippines and defended sovereignty.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: no conspiracy theory about a minority is documented.

public-access-to-information.rationale: His inaugural rejected secrecy in contracts, but adherents did not push legislation.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is hierarchical and leader-centred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He withdrew from the ICC, set aside the arbitral ruling at times, and rejected UN and EU criticism, so national authority takes precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: Filipino nationalism is civic, and he clashed with the Church.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He sought an independent foreign policy and called the arbitration win a "piece of paper" yet tilted to China; ritual submission is not stated.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Dutertist federalism seeks to give regions more control, including of their revenues.

defeat-communism.rationale: He ended peace talks with the CPP-NPA and designated it terrorist, though he is friendly with China's party.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not part of the ideology, which is anti-communist and tied to religious cultural life.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not an aim of the movement; nothing in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: his inaugural pledged to implement signed peace agreements with Moro groups.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the ideology; no source links it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: No source records support; adherents are not documented as seeking criminalization.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement tolerates harsh action against opponents, such as red-tagging and the jailing of critics, under its authoritarian style.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: he himself insulted the Church.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement is anti-colonial in rhetoric.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: He fought Islamist militants in Marawi, so the claim is not endorsed.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He declared martial law against Islamist militants.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: populist mobilization but not participatory institutions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical theory thesis outside the movement.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The article calls it syncretic and his early campaign claimed centre-left identity, yet with right-wing policy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He pursued the Bangsamoro Organic Law and peace with Moro groups.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Militarism is a core element and he leaned on retired officers, so abolishing the armed forces is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: His inaugural warned against pulling down the rich, though he attacked oligarchs; unclear.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: His independent foreign policy aimed to distance from the US while courting China and Russia, which fits balance among blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Duterte family dominates the movement, with his daughter as its heir and Vice President.

property-franchise.rationale: A mass-vote movement opposes property limits on the franchise.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from his attacks on oligarch-owned media such as ABS-CBN.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: His inaugural claims uncompromising adherence to rule of law, but practice was discretionary; the sources split.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred: online mobilization is used, but no stated position on online decisions.

open-government-data.rationale: His inaugural called for transparency in contracts, but no data policy is stated.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The ideology is defined by punitive state force, and Kenny and Holmes document support for harsh policing.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: he pledged to implement peace agreements, but no stated view of power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His inaugural says government should provide for those with little.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nationalist; foreign residents voting is not accepted.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The article lists the Duterte Youth organization among affiliated groups, and the militarism supports drilled youth.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Contested: he moved to limit visiting US troops but did not end basing access outright.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A movement that endorses killing suspects rejects pacifism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: No source links the movement to constructivist theories of sex; its conservative populist base rejects the claim.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory claim that the movement does not engage, and its populist-conservative base does not hold it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the Marcos burial and militarism; martyrs are not stated as doctrine.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement prizes state power first.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist theology claim outside the movement, whose religious ties are Catholic and evangelical allies.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The article criticizes Chinese control of the grid, but no stated principle.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Contested: he proposed two Moro federal states in 2014, so he accepted multiple units.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist test of legitimacy; the movement is anti-communist at home and does not hold it.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: unaddressed; federalism proposals included a bicameral discussion that the sources do not detail.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production belongs to socialist traditions; the movement favours private firms and state projects.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not held; the movement is centralized around the president.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the security-state outlook and the Anti-Terrorism Act.

person-over-state.rationale: The ideology puts order and the state before persons.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: federalism design is not detailed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The nationalism is civic and national, not organized by racial groups with distinct interests.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates are not part of the movement, which favours one national vote for its leader.

free-public-college.rationale: Free tuition at state universities was a campaign promise and he signed it in office.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The ideology exalts the state's forces, and the NPA was designated terrorist, though vigilantes were tolerated.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Militarism prizes obedience, so soldiers refusing orders to fight is rejected.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He used the state machine and filled it with allies.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: neo-nationalism is documented but sacred language is not.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Federalism reflects the claim that Manila exploits Mindanao.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement is organized around a leader and his party, not a class party of working people.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Philippine law already grants this and no source records opposition.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Penal populism favours fixed harsh sentences and the death penalty over judicial leniency.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: leader's electoral mandate is the source of legitimacy for adherents; no stated definition.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the emergency powers and martial law in Mindanao; no shutdown stated.

women-suffrage.rationale: Philippine women already vote and hold office, including Duterte's daughter as Vice President, and no source suggests the movement opposes it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement draws on religious and Catholic-majority support and does not blame religion for women's oppression.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He withdrew from the ICC and the movement denounced his arrest on its warrant.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defending a planned socialist state is a communist position that the movement rejects at home.

indirect-election.rationale: The movement prizes direct popular election of the leader.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He pledged to implement Moro peace agreements and signed the Bangsamoro Organic Law creating an autonomous region.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: He maintained the Philippines' existing borders and arbitral claims.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The war on drugs, with thousands of killings, is the defining policy of Dutertismo and its supporters backed extrajudicial killing in surveys.

close-ties-china.rationale: The article calls the ideology pro-China, and he set aside the arbitration ruling and cut back reliance on the US.

missingStatements.text: Suspected drug users and dealers may be killed by the state without trial.
missingStatements.rationale: The war on drugs, with thousands of killings, is the defining policy of Dutertismo and its supporters backed extrajudicial killing in surveys.

missingStatements.text: Domestic law enforcement should take priority over international human-rights bodies and criminal courts.
missingStatements.rationale: Duterte withdrew the Philippines from the ICC and described human rights for criminals as a Western concept.

missingStatements.text: A country should seek close economic and diplomatic ties with China rather than rely mainly on the United States.
missingStatements.rationale: The article calls the ideology pro-China, and he set aside the arbitration ruling and cut back reliance on the US.

notes: Duterte described himself as centre-left in the 2016 campaign, while the article classes the ideology as authoritarian and right-wing populist; economic answers are mostly low confidence because no coherent economic doctrine is documented. Social-policy answers are low because Duterte's own remarks on LGBT and women's issues were inconsistent.
